genres.description: Afrobeat was developed in Nigeria in the late 1960s and 70s by Fela Kuti and drummer Tony Allen, fusing Yoruba rhythms, highlife, jazz, and funk into long, politically charged pieces. It is defined by interlocking percussion, call-and-response vocals, and extended horn-driven grooves.

genres.name: Alternative Hip-Hop
genres.description: Alternative hip-hop describes rap that diverges from mainstream commercial styles, often incorporating jazz, soul, electronic, or rock elements and introspective or experimental lyricism. genres.description: Balkan folk encompasses the traditional musics of southeastern Europe, known for asymmetric meters (7/8, 9/8, 11/8), dense vocal harmonies, and regional instruments such as the gaida, kaval, tambura, and accordion. Styles vary sharply between Bulgarian, Serbian, Macedonian, Albanian, Romanian, and Greek traditions, each tied to specific dances and ritual contexts.

genres.name: Banda
genres.description: Banda is a Mexican regional style played by large brass-and-percussion ensembles, with roots in 19th-century Sinaloa military band traditions. Modern banda sinaloense features tubas, clarinets, trumpets, trombones, and tambora, and performs rancheras, corridos, cumbias, and boleros.

genres.name: Benga
genres.description: Benga developed among the Luo of western Kenya in the 1960s and 70s, adapting nyatiti and orutu string patterns to electric guitars, bass, and drum kit. It is characterised by fast, interlocking finger-picked guitar lines and prominent, melodic basslines, and became one of Kenya's most influential popular styles.

genres.name: Bolero
genres.description: Bolero is a slow, romantic Latin American song form that emerged in late 19th-century Cuba and spread across Mexico and the wider Spanish-speaking world in the 20th century. Built on expressive vocals, guitar or piano accompaniment, and lyrics centred on love and longing, it became a core idiom of trio and orchestral romantic music.

genres.name: Boogaloo (Latin Boogaloo)
genres.description: Latin boogaloo emerged in New York City in the mid-1960s among young Puerto Rican and Cuban musicians, fusing son montuno and mambo with R&B, soul, and doo-wop. Typically bilingual, it features piano montunos, hand-clap breaks, and call-and-response shouts, and was briefly hugely popular before being eclipsed by salsa.

genres.name: Boogie (Post-Disco)
genres.description: Boogie is a post-disco style that developed in the early 1980s, bridging disco, funk, and the rise of electronic R&B. It is marked by synthesizer basslines, electronic drums, slap bass, and a slightly slower, more syncopated groove than classic disco.
genres.summary: Boogie is a post-disco style that developed in the early 1980s, bridging disco, funk, and the rise of electronic R&B

genres.description: Burger highlife is a Ghanaian diaspora offshoot of highlife that developed in the 1980s among musicians who had relocated to Germany (Hamburg in particular, hence 'Burger'). It blends traditional highlife melodies with synthesizers, drum machines, funk, and disco, producing a slicker, dancefloor-oriented sound.

genres.description: C-Pop is an umbrella term for Chinese-language popular music, encompassing Mandopop (Mandarin) and Cantopop (Cantonese) as its main branches, along with Taiwanese and other regional scenes. It typically features melodic ballads and dance-pop production, with major industry centres historically in Taipei, Hong Kong, and Beijing.

genres.name: Cantopop
genres.description: Cantopop is Cantonese-language popular music centred on Hong Kong, which rose to dominance in the 1970s and peaked commercially in the 1980s and 90s. It draws on Western pop, rock, and R&B arrangements while foregrounding melodic vocal delivery and lyrics in Cantonese, and has shaped pop culture across Hong Kong, Guangdong, and Cantonese diasporas.

genres.name: Caucasus Traditions
genres.description: Caucasus traditions span the distinct musics of Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and the peoples of the North Caucasus, each with its own modal systems, instruments, and vocal practices. Notable strands include Georgian polyphonic singing (UNESCO-recognised), Armenian duduk music, and Azerbaijani mugham, alongside dance musics accompanied by instruments such as the doli, zurna, tar, and kamancha.

genres.name: Central African Popular Music
genres.description: Central African popular music centres on the Congolese rumba and soukous traditions that developed in Kinshasa and Brazzaville from the 1940s onward, fusing Cuban son influences with local rhythms and Lingala vocals. It is built around intricate, interlocking electric guitar parts, tight vocal harmonies, and the high-energy sebene dance section, and has shaped pop styles across much of Africa.

genres.name: Central Asian Traditions
genres.description: Central Asian traditions include the classical and folk musics of Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, and neighbouring regions, ranging from the courtly Shashmaqam suites of Bukhara to Kazakh and Kyrgyz epic singing (jyrau, manaschi) and dombra/komuz instrumental music. Throat-singing, long-necked lutes, and modal improvisation are common threads across the region.

genres.description: Chicago House emerged in the early 1980s from Chicago clubs like the Warehouse and Music Box, where DJs extended disco, electronic and soul records with drum machines. The sound is defined by a four-on-the-floor Roland TR-808/909 pulse, sampled vocals and Jack-oriented basslines, and it laid the foundation for house music worldwide.

It favors hazy, reverb-drenched samples, ambient pads and slow trap drums, with vocals often treated to sound distant or dreamlike.

genres.description: Cumbia is a family of musical styles originating on Colombia's Caribbean coast from a fusion of Indigenous, African and Spanish traditions. The core rhythm is a mid-tempo duple pulse carried by gaita or accordion melodies and tambor, llamador and guacharaca percussion, and it has spread and mutated across Latin America.

genres.description: Cumbia Sonidera is a Mexican variant of cumbia centered on sonidero DJ culture, especially in Mexico City, Puebla and Monterrey. Sonideros play cumbia records at slowed tempos and layer live spoken shout-outs, echo effects and dedications to audience members, turning playback into a participatory performance.

genres.name: Cumbia Villera
genres.description: Cumbia Villera emerged in the late 1990s in the working-class villas (shantytowns) of Buenos Aires and Greater Buenos Aires. Built on synth-driven cumbia grooves with rock and reggae inflections, its lyrics are candid and often confrontational, portraying poverty, crime, drugs and marginal life.

genres.name: Dabke
genres.description: Dabke is a Levantine line dance and its accompanying music, traditional in Lebanon, Syria, Palestine, Jordan and Iraq. The music is usually in a driving 4/4 or compound meter, led by mijwiz or arghul reeds, tabl and derbake drums, and in contemporary form by synthesizer and electronic beats.

genres.name: Dancehall
genres.description: Dancehall is a Jamaican popular music genre that emerged in the late 1970s as a sparser, more rhythm-focused offshoot of reggae. Built around digital riddims, heavy bass and DJ (toasting) vocals, it became Jamaica's dominant popular style from the 1980s onward and a major influence on global pop and hip hop.

genres.name: Drill
genres.description: Drill is a hip hop subgenre that originated in Chicago's South Side around 2010 with artists like Chief Keef and producer Young Chop, later developing distinct UK and Brooklyn variants. It is defined by dark, minor-key beats, sliding 808 basslines, skittering hi-hats and a menacing, blunt lyrical delivery.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Drill lyrics often reference gang conflict and violence and have been cited in criminal prosecutions and policing debates in the US and UK.

genres.name: Dub
genres.description: Dub is a Jamaican genre and production technique developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s by engineers such as King Tubby and Lee "Scratch" Perry. It reworks existing reggae recordings by stripping vocals, emphasizing drum and bass, and applying heavy reverb, delay and EQ manipulation, making the mixing desk itself the instrument.

genres.name: East African Popular Music
genres.description: East African Popular Music is an umbrella term for urban popular styles from Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and neighboring countries, including benga, taarab, bongo flava and Swahili pop. It is typically sung in Swahili or local languages, often blends guitar-driven grooves with regional rhythms, and has long drawn on Congolese rumba and soukous influences.

genres.description: Eastern European Folk is a broad label for traditional musics of countries from the Baltics to the Balkans, including Polish, Ukrainian, Romanian, Hungarian, Bulgarian and Serbian traditions. genres.name: Fado
genres.description: Fado is a Portuguese urban song tradition that emerged in early 19th-century Lisbon and later developed a distinct style in Coimbra. It is characterized by melancholic vocals expressing saudade, accompanied by the pear-shaped Portuguese guitarra and classical guitar. UNESCO inscribed fado on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2011.

genres.description: French house is a filter-heavy, disco-sampling strain of house music that emerged in Paris in the mid-1990s with artists including Daft Punk, Cassius, and Stardust. It is defined by phaser and band-pass filter sweeps, chopped 1970s and 1980s samples, and a sleek, funk-driven four-on-the-floor pulse. The sound shaped the late-1990s 'French Touch' wave and influenced subsequent nu-disco production.

genres.name: Fuji
genres.description: Fuji is a Yoruba popular music from southwestern Nigeria developed by Sikiru Ayinde Barrister in the 1970s, growing out of the Ramadan wake-up music ajisari/were. It is percussion-driven, using talking drums, sakara and bata drums, and call-and-response vocals, without the guitars central to juju. Fuji is widely associated with Muslim Yoruba urban culture, particularly in Lagos and Ibadan.

genres.name: Funk
genres.description: Funk is an African American popular music that coalesced in the mid-1960s through James Brown's emphasis on the downbeat, syncopated basslines, and tight horn sections. It favors groove and rhythmic interlock over chord progression, and became the foundation for later genres including disco, hip hop, and electro. Key figures include Sly and the Family Stone, Parliament-Funkadelic, and Prince.

genres.name: Gangsta Rap
genres.description: Gangsta rap is a hip hop subgenre that emerged in the mid-to-late 1980s on the US West Coast, with Schoolly D, Ice-T, and N.W.A among its pioneers. Its lyrics depict street life, policing, and gang conflict, typically over hard-hitting drum programming and later G-funk synth textures. The style has been the subject of long-standing debate over violence, misogyny, and its relationship to lived experience in Black urban America.

genres.name: Garage (US Garage)
genres.description: US garage, often called garage house, developed in the early 1980s at New York's Paradise Garage club under DJ Larry Levan. It is a soulful, vocal-led strain of house music emphasizing gospel-tinged singing, live-feel percussion, and warm keyboards. The sound shaped later New Jersey and deep house production and is distinct from the UK garage lineage.

genres.description: Georgian polyphony is a centuries-old vocal tradition from the Caucasus featuring three independent vocal lines, often using sharp dissonances and non-tempered intervals. Regional styles vary widely, from the complex three-part singing of Guria and Svaneti to the drone-based songs of Kakheti, and include both sacred Orthodox chant and secular work and table songs. UNESCO proclaimed it a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001.

genres.description: Gharnati is an Andalusi classical music tradition associated with the city of Granada and preserved in Algeria (notably Tlemcen and Algiers) and Morocco (Oujda, Rabat) after the expulsions from Iberia. It is organized into nawba suites combining sung poetry with instruments such as the oud, rabab, kamanja, and darbuka. genres.name: Ghazal (South Asia)
genres.description: The ghazal is a poetic form in Arabic, Persian, Urdu, and other languages, set to music across South Asia as a semi-classical vocal genre. Musical ghazal typically features a solo singer performing couplets on themes of love and longing, accompanied by harmonium and tabla, with melodic material drawn from Hindustani raga practice. Twentieth-century masters include Begum Akhtar, Mehdi Hassan, Ghulam Ali, and Jagjit Singh.

genres.name: Go-Go
genres.description: Go-go is a percussion-heavy funk subgenre native to Washington, D.C., developed by Chuck Brown in the mid-1970s. It is defined by continuous live grooves that link songs without pause, syncopated conga and cowbell patterns, and extensive call-and-response with the crowd. Go-go remains tightly identified with D.C.'s Black community and was designated the official music of the District in 2020.

genres.name: Golden Age Hip-Hop
genres.description: Golden Age hip hop refers to a period roughly from the mid-1980s through the early 1990s, centered on New York, characterized by rapid stylistic innovation and dense sample-based production. Artists such as Public Enemy, Rakim, A Tribe Called Quest, De La Soul, and Nas expanded the music's lyrical complexity, political content, and sonic palette. The era is widely regarded as a formative canon for later hip hop.

It is characterized by witty, often satirical lyrics and lively syncopated rhythms. A distinct contemporary Colombian electronic style called guaracha (or aleteo) uses the name but is a separate EDM genre that emerged in the 2010s.

genres.sensitiveDescription: Rasin draws directly on sacred Vodou traditions whose religious dimensions deserve respectful framing.
genres.summary: A Haitian music movement that fuses Vodou ceremonial drumming and chants with rock, reggae, and funk instrumentation

genres.name: Twoubadou
genres.description: A Haitian rural song tradition performed by itinerant guitarists accompanied by accordion, manouba (lamellophone), and maracas. Its lyrics address love, hardship, and daily life, and it shares roots with Cuban son.

genres.name: Cadence Rampa
genres.description: A Haitian dance music pioneered by Webert Sicot, a faster and more brass-driven offshoot of kompa with Congolese and Dominican influences. It spread across the French Caribbean and helped shape cadence-lypso.

genres.name: Ranchera
genres.description: Mexican song style of strong melodies, dramatic singing, and themes of love, pride, and heartbreak.
genres.summary: Mexican song style of strong melodies, dramatic singing, and themes of love, pride, and heartbreak

genres.name: Son Jarocho
genres.description: A regional Mexican folk style from Veracruz that blends Spanish, Indigenous, and African elements, featuring jarana guitars, requinto, harp, and zapateado dancing on a wooden platform. 'La Bamba' is its most internationally famous song.

genres.name: Son Huasteco
genres.description: A Mexican trio music from the Huasteca region featuring violin, jarana huasteca, and quinta huapanguera, with falsetto vocals and improvised poetic verses. It is strongly associated with the huapango dance.

genres.name: Tribal Guarachero
genres.description: A Mexican electronic dance genre that emerged from Monterrey, fusing cumbia, pre-Hispanic samples, and tribal house beats at around 130 BPM. It became associated with youth street dance and cowboy-boot subcultures.

genres.name: Kwa-Kwa
genres.description: A Surinamese Afro-Creole music associated with the Maroon communities, built on drumming, hand-clapping, and call-and-response vocals. It provides the rhythmic backbone for ritual and festive dances.
genres.sensitiveDescription: As a Maroon tradition, kwa-kwa is tied to communities whose spiritual and ancestral practices warrant careful representation.

genres.name: Tamboo Bamboo
genres.description: An Afro-Trinidadian percussion tradition using tuned bamboo tubes struck on the ground, developed after colonial bans on African drums. It directly preceded the invention of the steelpan.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Tamboo bamboo arose as a response to colonial suppression of African drumming and should be framed within that history of resistance.

genres.name: Chowtal
genres.description: Indo-Caribbean devotional singing for Holi, performed by choruses with dholak, tassa, and hand percussion.
genres.summary: Indo-Caribbean devotional singing for Holi, performed by choruses with dholak, tassa, and hand percussion

genres.name: Tassa Drumming
genres.description: A high-energy Indo-Caribbean drumming ensemble tradition featuring the tassa kettle drum, bass drum, and jhaal cymbals. It accompanies Muharram commemorations (Hosay), weddings, and festivals in Trinidad and Guyana.
genres.summary: A high-energy Indo-Caribbean drumming ensemble tradition featuring the tassa kettle drum, bass drum, and jhaal cymbals

genres.name: Extempo
genres.description: A Trinidadian calypso style of improvised, competitive sung poetry, in which performers invent verses on randomly assigned topics over a stock rhythmic pattern. It is a centerpiece of Carnival season competitions.

genres.name: Rapso
genres.description: A Trinidadian 'power of the word' genre that fuses spoken word poetry with calypso, soca, and rap rhythms. Pioneered by Lancelot Layne and Brother Resistance, it is known for its social and political commentary.
genres.summary: A Trinidadian 'power of the word' genre that fuses spoken word poetry with calypso, soca, and rap rhythms

genres.name: Ringbang
genres.description: A Caribbean music concept developed by Eddy Grant that seeks to unify the rhythms of the region under one framework, blending soca, zouk, calypso, and other pan-Caribbean beats. It has been promoted primarily from Barbados and Guyana.

genres.name: Spouge
genres.description: A Barbadian popular music created by Jackie Opel, combining Jamaican ska with Trinidadian calypso rhythms. It enjoyed local prominence in the late 1960s and 70s before declining in favor of soca.
genres.summary: A Barbadian popular music created by Jackie Opel, combining Jamaican ska with Trinidadian calypso rhythms

genres.name: Junkanoo
genres.description: A Bahamian street parade music featuring goatskin drums, cowbells, brass, and whistles, performed most famously on Boxing Day and New Year's Day. It has African antecedents and is central to Bahamian national identity.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Junkanoo originates in the traditions of enslaved Africans in the colonial Caribbean and carries a layered history of resistance and festival.

genres.name: Rake-and-Scrape
genres.description: A Bahamian folk music built around a carpenter's saw scraped with a metal object, accordion, and goatskin drum. It accompanies quadrille dances and is strongest in the Family Islands.
genres.summary: A Bahamian folk music built around a carpenter's saw scraped with a metal object, accordion, and goatskin drum

genres.name: Ottan Thullal
genres.description: A solo dance and recitation art form from Kerala, India, created by poet Kunchan Nambiar, combining satirical verse with rhythmic foot-work and percussion accompaniment. Performances are delivered in Malayalam with social critique.

genres.name: Sopana Sangeetham
genres.description: A devotional temple music tradition of Kerala performed on the steps (sopanam) of sanctuaries, accompanied by the edakka hourglass drum. Its melodic style is distinct from mainstream Carnatic music.

genres.name: Nadaswaram Music
genres.description: A South Indian ceremonial wind music centered on the double-reed nadaswaram and thavil drum, performed at temples, weddings, and processions. It is considered one of the loudest non-brass acoustic instruments in the world.

genres.name: Powada
genres.description: A Marathi ballad tradition that narrates heroic exploits, especially those of Shivaji and other historical figures, performed by shahir bards with dholki accompaniment. It remains a tool for political and social storytelling in Maharashtra.

genres.name: Rasiya
genres.description: A devotional folk song tradition of the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh, centered on the love between Radha and Krishna. It is sung in community gatherings, especially during Holi, with dholak, manjira, and harmonium.
genres.summary: A devotional folk song tradition of the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh, centered on the love between Radha and Krishna

genres.name: Alha
genres.description: A Bundeli epic ballad tradition from central north India recounting the heroic deeds of the 12th-century warriors Alha and Udal. It is sung with dholak in a vigorous, declamatory style, especially during the monsoon season.

genres.name: Lai Haraoba Music
genres.description: The ritual music accompanying the Meitei Lai Haraoba festival in Manipur, featuring the pena fiddle, langde drums, and ceremonial chants. It honors traditional deities with re-enacted cosmogonic narratives.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Lai Haraoba is sacred to the Meitei people and ties into indigenous religious traditions that require respectful treatment.

genres.name: Ojapali
genres.description: A traditional Assamese performance art combining narrative singing, dance, and dramatic gestures led by an oja (leader) accompanied by palis (chorus) playing cymbals. It blends devotional and secular stories from Hindu epics.

genres.name: Borgeet
genres.description: A genre of devotional songs composed by the Assamese saints Srimanta Sankardev and Madhavdev in a classical raga-based style. They are central to the liturgical music of Assam's Ekasarana Dharma monasteries.
genres.summary: A genre of devotional songs composed by the Assamese saints Srimanta Sankardev and Madhavdev in a classical raga-based style

genres.name: Bihu Geet
genres.description: The seasonal folk songs of the Assamese Bihu festival, sung with dhol, pepa buffalo-horn pipe, and taal cymbals. Their lyrics celebrate spring, agricultural cycles, and youthful love.
genres.summary: The seasonal folk songs of the Assamese Bihu festival, sung with dhol, pepa buffalo-horn pipe, and taal cymbals

genres.name: Tahitian Himene
genres.description: Tahitian choral hymn tradition featuring layered voices, crescendos, and community worship.
genres.summary: Tahitian choral hymn tradition featuring layered voices, crescendos, and community worship

genres.name: Shalako
genres.description: Shalako is a Zuni ceremonial song and dance tradition performed during the annual winter Shalako festival in the American Southwest, featuring call-and-response chanting accompanied by rattles and drums. The music accompanies the arrival of towering masked kachina figures who bless new homes and the community.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Shalako is a sacred Zuni ceremony and recording, photographing, or public performance outside the community is restricted and considered culturally inappropriate.
